newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann wins pay TV rights to soccer.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann wins pay TV rights to soccer.

text.p: Bertelsmann AG, the German media giant, has won the exclusive pay TV rights to broadcast live German first division soccer matches for the 1996/97 and 1997/98 seasons, the company's chairman said late on Monday.

Mark Woessner told members of the Foreign Press Association in Germany that the company's television unit Ufa Film- und Fernseh GmbH would hold both the conventional pay TV rights and the digital pay TV rights to broadcast two live games a week.

"The deal is exclusive. No third party can come in and buy rights to broadcast any other soccer matches," Woessner said in a clear reference to Bertelsmann pay TV rival Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch.
"This secures the rights to soccer for Ufa and thereby for Premiere," he said.
Premiere is the pay TV channel that is jointly-owned by Bertelsmann, Canal Plus and Kirch. But Kirch earlier this year launched a competing digital pay TV channel called DF1.

Bertelsmann has launched a legal challenge against Kirch, because it says he is intentionally seeking to damage Premiere, which could be seen as a violation of his contract with the company as 25 percent shareholder.
Bertelsmann and Canal Plus, the French pay TV group, each own 37.5 percent of Premiere.
Premiere, long the only pay TV channel in Germany, has around 1.35 million subscribers currently and expects to reach 1.4 million by the end of the year.
"Premiere now has a net gain of 10,000 new subscribers a week," Woessner said.
Woessner said he signed the contracts for the soccer rights on October 20 with the German Soccer Federation (DFB).
Bertelsmann has an option to take up the rights for another three seasons after the end of the 1997/98 season. Woessner gave no financial details.
